criteria.criterion: The ownership question is answerable BEFORE an amend or submit, by a documented and scripted check rather than by an agent happening to think of it.

A submit is refused, or at minimum loudly warned, when the current_revision differs from the revision whose votes were inspected. Proven by attempting a submit against a deliberately stale revision and observing the refusal.

The interaction with vote invalidation is stated wherever the push flow is documented: an unnecessary patch set RESETS LLM-Review and Verified to Outdated and re-queues the change, so re-pushing a green change is destructive, not neutral.

Whichever direction is chosen is recorded with its reasoning, including an explicit decision on per-session identities (adopt or reject with a reason) rather than defaulting to the cheapest option by omission.
Bug 'Concurrent sessions share one RebarBotNava Gerrit identity…' is actually resolved

findings.criterion: The interaction with vote invalidation is stated wherever the push flow is documented: an unnecessary patch set RESETS LLM-Review and Verified to Outdated and re-queues the change, so re-pushing a green change is destructive, not neutral.
findings.detail: Searched CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, and docs/releasing.md for all relevant phrases: 'vote invalidation', 'Outdated', 're-pushing', 'destructive', 'RESETS', 're-queues', 'marks prior votes', 'not neutral', 'unnecessary patch set'. None of the push-flow documentation sections contain the required statement that an unnecessary patch set resets LLM-Review and Verified to Outdated and re-queues the change. CONTRIBUTING.md §2e (lines 284-301) and AGENTS.md (lines 437-475) cover the revision-scoped submit and session hashtags but omit this vote-invalidation warning entirely.
findings.title: Vote-invalidation warning missing from push-flow documentation

findings.criterion: Whichever direction is chosen is recorded with its reasoning, including an explicit decision on per-session identities (adopt or reject with a reason) rather than defaulting to the cheapest option by omission.
findings.detail: The chosen approach (revision-scoped submit + session hashtag) is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md §2e and AGENTS.md, but no explicit decision text on per-session Gerrit identities (adopt or reject with a stated reason) was found anywhere in the repository files. The operator constraint ('all sessions share one credential; per-session identities rejected') appears only in the ticket comments, not in any codebase documentation (CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, docs/releasing.md, or an ADR). The criterion requires this decision to be recorded in the documentation, not just in the ticket.
findings.title: Explicit per-session identity decision not recorded in codebase docs

findings.criterion: Bug 'Concurrent sessions share one RebarBotNava Gerrit identity…' is actually resolved
findings.detail: The core submit-race hazard is addressed by the revision-scoped submit script and GerritClient methods. However, two of the four acceptance criteria are unmet (vote-invalidation warning in push-flow docs; explicit per-session identity decision recorded with reasoning), so the bug's own acceptance criteria are not fully satisfied and the bug cannot be considered fully resolved.
findings.title: Bug partially resolved — two acceptance criteria unmet

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
